text: The accretion of lean mass depends on meeting daily dietary protein needs. The RDA for protein is 0.8 g/kg of body mass. This recommendation is based on research showing that such an amount is sufficient for 98% of healthy, non-exercising adults to remain in a non-negative nitrogen balance. However, the RDA, although adequate for those who are largely sedentary, cannot be generalized to a resistance-trained population, particularly those who aspire to maximize muscle development. For one, the maintenance of nitrogen balance indicates that day-to-day protein losses are offset by the synthesis of new bodily proteins; gaining muscle requires a positive nitrogen balance (i.e., protein synthesis exceeds degradation over time).
